finding: Slovak turnover expectations fell sharply while EA firms remained optimistic
bullets: A net 6.75% of Slovak firms (n=228) expected turnover to increase over the next two quarters, down 14.15 pp from two quarters earlier, against a net 25.88% for the euro area (n=5,266) — signalling weaker domestic demand.

Slovak fixed investment expectations rose to a net 14.67% (n=228), up 3.88 pp from two quarters earlier, outpacing the euro area's net 9.45% and Germany's net -2.42% — suggesting some firms are betting on future growth despite current headwinds.

The 19.1 pp gap between Slovak and euro area turnover expectations points to diverging near-term growth trajectories, with Slovak firms' revenue outlook the weakest among the three economies compared.
